editorial:
If you love a good survival thriller where the hunted becomes the hunter, Apex delivers exactly that kind of ride. The story follows Thomas Malone, a former cop locked up for a crime he didn't commit, who gets a shot at freedom by surviving a deadly game on a remote island. Six wealthy hunters pay big money for the thrill of tracking a human, and Malone is their target. The setup is simple but effective, and the island setting gives the whole thing a tense, gritty feel. You never quite know who to trust, and the action keeps coming at a steady pace.

The movie leans heavily on its action scenes, which are loud and frequent, though not always polished. Bruce Willis brings his usual tough-guy energy, and the supporting cast does enough to keep things moving. The pacing is fast, sometimes too fast, skipping over character moments you might want more of. Still, if you are in the mood for a no-nonsense action flick with a survival twist, this one is worth a look.
endingExplained: In the final act, Malone turns the tables on the hunters one by one, using the island's terrain to his advantage. The twist comes when you learn the game was rigged from the start, with the prison warden secretly involved in the betting. Malone confronts the last hunter and the warden, surviving the final showdown. He escapes the island and clears his name, walking free as the credits roll. It is a satisfying, if predictable, ending that rewards you for sticking with the chaos.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves action-packed survival thrillers with a tough-guy lead.
